parts.note: to scarper is to run off, which in British slang is to leg it
one is the Roman numeral I
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it is all right to run off with a pal.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'leg it' is British slang for running away, matching 'Scarper'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something legitimate is lawful and acceptable, which is what OK says informally.

parts.note: militant suggests soldiers, so farmers organised like an army: the wartime body of women sent to work British farms

explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Land Army recruited British women to work on farms during the two World Wars; 'Militant' plays on its army name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Women's Land Army was a uniformed wartime organisation of farm workers, so its members were farmers in military style.

clue.text: Good many in a split skirt, for example

indicators.note: in says the letter for many goes inside the word for split

parts.note: a rent is a split or tear
M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many

explanation.surface: A skirt with a slit in it, worn by plenty of people.
explanation.walkthrough: M for 'many' comes from the Roman thousand; 'in' puts it inside RENT, after G and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirt is one example of an item of clothing.

clue.text: Change? RAF man isn't too worried about resistance

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go round the letter for resistance
worried letters are fretted and shaken up, so RAF MAN ISN'T TOO is rearranged

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An airman claims not to be overly bothered about opposition to some change.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks 'Change?' as the definition; 'worried' is the anagram signal and 'about' the container signal, with R the usual symbol for electrical resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A transformation is a thorough alteration in form or character.

indicators.note: accepting means the word for union takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a merger is a union of two firms
A is a musical key
N and S are compass points, north and south

explanation.surface: A divers' association takes on some important matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diver' is a diving duck, not a person; 'accepting' puts A plus N and S inside MERGER.
explanation.definitionFit: The merganser is a fish-eating duck that hunts by diving, so it is a diver.

clue.text: Army escorting a political representative in US resort

indicators.note: escorting suggests the army flanks the other letters on both sides

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, the British reserve force
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Troops guard a member of parliament visiting a holiday spot in America.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve; 'escorting' signals that it surrounds the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampa is a Florida city known as a holiday destination.

indicators.note: contains says the answer is held within the run of letters of muesli packaging

explanation.surface: A complaint that the cereal box has a mistake on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' looks like the link to the definition but signals the letters muesLI Packaging running across the word join.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small mistake.

clue.text: Dissembles about drink? That's an understatement

indicators.note: about says the word for dissembles goes round the drink

parts.note: to dissemble is to deceive, as one who lies does
a tot is a small drink of spirits

explanation.surface: Calling someone a liar who has had a drink is putting it mildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is a figure of speech that makes a point by deliberate understatement, as in 'not bad'.

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
racy means daring or risque

explanation.surface: A Greek man commits a bold offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Piracy is robbery at sea, or illegal copying, both crimes.

parts.note: taken as a horse leaping obstacles too hastily, but it means acting before thinking

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from horse riding: a rider who goes at the obstacles too fast risks a fall, hence acting rashly.
explanation.definitionFit: To act hastily, like a horse taking obstacles too fast, is to leap before being ready.

clue.text: Mean to put on amateur opera

indicators.note: to put on says the amateur letter is added to the end of the word for mean

parts.note: a norm is a mean or average

explanation.surface: An instruction to stage an amateur production of an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: NORMA is an opera by Bellini.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is Bellini's tragic opera about a Druid priestess.

parts.note: a cake made tipsy is laced with alcohol, so its filling would be a sweet spread made with spirit

explanation.walkthrough: A tipsy cake is a British dessert of sponge soaked in alcohol; the filling would be boozy too.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum butter is a sweet spread of butter, sugar and rum, apt for a cake that is drunk.

definitions.meaning: a verb meaning to pester persistently

explanation.definitionFit: A nag is an old or worn-out horse; to badger someone is to nag them.

indicators.note: initially ignored says the first letter of the birds is dropped

parts.note: ravens are large black birds

explanation.surface: A plant that dark birds have taken no notice of from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the first letter of RAVENS leaves the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Avens is a flowering herb of the rose family, also called herb bennet.

clue.text: African leader affecting to be indifferent

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: affecting means moving, which is the original sense of pathetic

explanation.surface: An African head of state pretends to be unconcerned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affecting' here is an adjective meaning moving, not 'pretending'; PATHETIC still has that older sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathetic means showing no interest or concern.

parts.note: read as continuing, but meant as an illness that strikes while on the go, travelling

explanation.walkthrough: 'On-going' usually means continuing; split, it means while going somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Travel sickness is an ailment caused by movement in cars, ships or planes.

clue.text: About to drop phone with a squeak?

parts.note: C stands for circa, about
to drop a point is to lose it
to call is to phone

explanation.surface: Someone about to let a phone fall makes a squeaking noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'with' are link words. A narrow squeak is a near miss.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow squeak, a lucky escape, is the same as a near miss.

clue.text: Lay there in bad state? Tough

indicators.note: in bad state says the letters of lay there are in disorder and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lay there in a poor condition and was hardy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in bad state' rearranges LAY THERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Leathery meat or skin is hard and tough like leather.

indicators.note: making signals that the letters of customers smile are being made into something new

explanation.surface: A summer's day long enough to make shoppers cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' rearranges CUSTOMERS SMILE.
explanation.definitionFit: The summer solstice has the most daylight of any day in the year.

clue.text: Signs of hesitation about mixing in a metal

indicators.note: about says the two hesitation sounds go round the mixed letters

parts.note: ur is a sound made while hesitating
um is another sound made while hesitating

indicators.note: mixing says the letters of in a are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates over blending in some metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixing' is the anagram signal and 'about' the container signal; UR and UM are both written hesitation noises.
explanation.definitionFit: Uranium is a radioactive metallic element used as nuclear fuel.

definitions.meaning: first or at the very start
a verb meaning to put one's name or mark on something

explanation.definitionFit: Initial means first or original; to initial a document is to sign it with one's initials.

clue.text: Attacks on king forming a pattern

definitions.meaning: chess moves that threaten the king directly
a design of squares, as on a tablecloth

explanation.surface: Raids on a monarch fall into a repeating design.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, moves threatening the king are checks; a checked fabric has a square pattern.

clue.text: Wild cheetah crossing a river in distress

indicators.note: crossing says the rearranged letters lie across, round, the other letters
wild means the letters of cheetah run free in a new order

explanation.surface: A wild big cat in trouble while crossing a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' is the anagram signal and 'crossing' puts the river pieces inside the rearranged cat, splitting it after the second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartache is emotional anguish or grief.

indicators.note: in says the letter for run goes inside the word for ready money

parts.note: the ready is British slang for cash
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Someone runs in, ready to fall down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is a noun: 'the readies' is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: To crash is to fall down or fail suddenly.

indicators.note: reflecting, as in a mirror, means the word for struggle is turned back to front

parts.note: to toil is to labour or struggle

explanation.surface: An English poet thinks about his battles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflecting' signals a reversal, as a mirror turns a word round; the poet is T. S. Eliot.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot was a celebrated poet, author of The Waste Land.

clue.text: Do one out of a bit

indicators.note: out of says the letter for one is removed from the coin

parts.note: a bit is a small coin, as in the old British threepenny bit
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Cheat someone of a little.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bit' was a coin, as in the old British threepenny bit; 'out of' removes I.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is to swindle or cheat them.

parts.note: a chip is a counter used in gambling

indicators.note: milling about, like a jostling crowd, says the letters move into a new order

parts.note: the letters of a lot are the anagram fodder, which as printed lack the second A the setter needed

explanation.surface: A crowd moves around the food counter.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, 'a lot' rearranged gives only four of the five letters after CHIP; a second A is missing from the clue. A chipolata is a small sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipolata is a small thin sausage often served as a cocktail nibble.

clue.text: The Italian's trapped in S American guerrilla country

indicators.note: trapped in says the Italian article is enclosed by the guerrilla's name

parts.note: Che Guevara was an Argentine revolutionary guerrilla
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian is held captive in guerrilla territory in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'S American' looks like part of the definition but belongs to the guerrilla, Che Guevara.
explanation.definitionFit: Chile is a nation on the west coast of South America.

indicators.note: hear of says the word for problem is to be listened to, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: Someone learns that a few have a difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear of' signals a sound-alike: SUM sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Some means an unspecified small number, a few.

definitions.meaning: fun for those in their minority, still legally children

explanation.surface: A show for the few turns out to be easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minority' means being under age, not a small group.
explanation.definitionFit: Children's games are entertainment of minority, being under age; also any very easy task.
